title: Ersa Core API
description: The Core request/response API (PROTO-CORE-API): newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 between the Interface and Core. Each method has a `<method>.params` and a `<method>.result` definition; each notification a `<method>.notification` definition. Objects are closed (additionalProperties: false) except settings and the shapes reserved for later milestones. Agent events are not copied here: session.event carries an envelope from agent-events.schema.json by reference.

request_id.description: The JSON-RPC id; Core echoes it.

oneOf.description: The handshake; must be the first request on a connection (PROTO-CORE-API-R01).
Stops all sessions cleanly; Core exits after answering.
Reserved: remote hosts are milestone M4.

Takes effect on the next start.

response.description: Core's answer to one request. Validate `result` against the `<method>.result` definition of the request's method.

id.description: null when the request's id could not be read.

code.description: -32000 for application errors; the standard JSON-RPC codes (-32700, -32600, -32601, -32602, -32603) for protocol-level failures.

index.description: With attachment_refused: the place in session.send's attachments of the attachment refused.

name.description: The backend's name, such as claude-code.

version.description: Absent when the backend is not installed or its version could not be read.

label.description: The backend's own display name, such as Claude Code.

version.description: Absent when the backend is not installed or its version could not be read.

tested.description: The oldest and newest backend versions the adapter was tested with.

models.description: The models a session can start with.

efforts.description: The efforts a session can start with.

permission_modes.description: The permission modes a session can start with.

choice.description: One value a session can start with. The choices are the adapter's knowledge of its tested versions, not detected on the host.

id.description: What session.create takes and session.list reports.

default.description: Whether a new session starts with this one when none is named.

path.description: The project's root, as a path on its host.

trusted.description: Whether the user trusts the project, so its own configuration loads in its sessions (ADR 0018). False unless project.add or project.set_trust said otherwise.

kind.description: root: the project's own folder, one per project, listed first. isolated: a checkout made for sessions.

path.description: The workspace's root, as a path on the project's host.

vcs_ref.description: The branch (git) an isolated workspace has checked out; empty for the root workspace.

name.description: The local branch's short name, such as main or feature/rail.

default.description: The repository's default branch: the one origin/HEAD points at, else main, else master, else the checked-out branch. At most one is.

uncommitted.description: Files with changes not committed, untracked files included.

ignored.description: Ignored entries the version control reports, a wholly ignored folder as one.

unshared.description: Commits reachable from the workspace's checkout, its branch or its own reflog that no other local branch or remote-tracking branch holds.

stranded.description: Those unshared commits the workspace's branch does not hold, which deleting the folder loses.

sessions.description: Sessions using the workspace, leaving out any marked deleting.

unrecorded.description: Whether git has lost its record of the workspace: its checkout and reflog went with it, so commits made on a detached checkout can't be counted.

token.description: Opaque; changes whenever the uncommitted files or their content, the unshared commits, the set of ignored entries or the counted sessions change. session.delete carries it.

workspace_changes.description: What deleting an isolated workspace would lose.

model.description: The model session.create was given, an id from backend.list. Absent when left out: the backend's own default.

effort.description: The effort session.create was given, an id from backend.list. Absent when left out: the backend's own default.

permission_mode.description: The permission mode the session started with: the one session.create was given, else the backend's default, which is always stated to it.

last_event_seq.description: Absent when the session has no events yet.

sending.description: Absent unless a send is under way: its phase.

archived.description: Whether the user archived the session. session.send to an archived session answers invalid_state; a refused session.resume leaves it archived; Core clears it only once it accepts a resume.

pinned.description: Whether the user pinned the session. Core stores it; session.arrange sets it.

section_id.description: The section the user put the session in, from section.list; absent when in none. Core stores it; session.arrange sets it, and section.remove clears it.

last_activity_at.description: When the session's latest turn ended. Core records it as a turn ends and changes it at no other time; absent until a turn has ended.

deleting.description: Absent unless the session is marked deleting: running while Core works on its delete, failed after a step failed, until a new session.delete finishes it. session.resume, session.send, session.set_archived, session.arrange and session.remove answer invalid_state while it is set.

section.description: A section the user made to group sessions in the rail.

state.description: The session's lifecycle state, so the rail follows it without subscribing.

tile.description: What the rail renders for a session; Core keeps it current from events. Usage fields are absent until known.

send_phase.description: Where a send is: checking its attachments, copying them into the session's scratch folder, waiting for a starting backend, or handing the message to the backend.

attachment.description: A file, image or folder sent with a message: by absolute path on the session's host, or a pasted image as base64 data.

line.description: The line verbatim, without its terminator.

settings.description: User settings, an open JSON object. Known keys: workspaces.root (string), the directory new worktrees go under.

client.description: What is attaching, such as the Shell or a test client.

api_versions.description: Every Core API version the client speaks.

api_version.description: The highest version both sides speak.

event_projection_version.description: The agent event schema version (`v`) this Core produces.

platform.description: The operating system Core runs on: windows, macos, or linux.

host.add.params.description: Reserved for milestone M4; the shape is decided then.

trusted.description: The user's answer when adding the project: whether its own configuration may load in its sessions. Untrusted when absent.

project.find.result.description: The project on the host whose folder is path, compared as project.add compares folders, or null.

name.description: Branch name for a git worktree; Core picks one when absent.

base.description: Any revision git resolves (a branch, tag, commit or main~1) that the workspace starts from; the default branch branch.list marks, else the checked-out commit, when absent.

branch.list.result.description: The project's local branches, sorted by name.

model.description: An id from backend.list; left to the backend when absent.

effort.description: An id from backend.list; left to the backend when absent.

permission_mode.description: An id from backend.list; left to the backend when absent.

archived.description: Archiving stops a live session first, as session.stop does.

pinned.description: Pins or unpins the session; left as it was when absent.

section_id.description: Puts the session in this section, or in none when null; left as it was when absent. A section that does not exist answers not_found.

session.arrange.params.description: Changes the fields given and leaves the others. A session marked deleting answers invalid_state.

token.description: The token of the workspace.changes the user was shown. Needed for a session in an isolated workspace: when what would be lost now differs, the delete is refused with invalid_state and the new workspace.changes, as JSON text, in detail. Ignored for a root workspace.

session.delete.params.description: The user's Delete: stops the session, deletes its isolated workspace's folder and branch when no other session uses the workspace and the branch holds no commit only it holds, deletes its record from its backend, and removes it. While it runs, requests that would change the session or its workspace answer invalid_state with detail busy.

workspace_deleted.description: Whether this delete took the session's workspace's folder, and its branch unless kept. Its row goes with it once no other session refers to it; a session whose delete kept the files, when the last to leave a workspace whose folder is gone, takes the row.

branch_kept.description: Whether the workspace's branch was kept because it holds commits no other branch or remote holds, or another worktree has it checked out. False when the workspace stayed.

attachments.description: In the order the user added them.

turn.description: The turn the message starts or joins; absent when Core has not projected the message yet.

workspace_id.description: The workspace the attachment is for, whose host reads the path; the result then says whether sending would copy it. Exactly one of this and host_id.

host_id.description: The host that reads the path, for a workspace not made yet.

lines.description: A text file's line count, for one of at most 10 MB.

media_type.description: For an image, told by its first bytes.

copied.description: Whether a send would copy it into the workspace's scratch folder: true for a file or folder whose target, resolved as a send resolves it, is outside workspace_id, or for any file or folder given a host_id; false for an image, which goes inline, and for a path inside the workspace.

updated_input.description: Replacement tool input; the tool's own arguments.

last_seq.description: Absent when the session has no events yet.

view.description: The identity of the view the subscription reads. When it differs from the view a client's events came from, they no longer line up, and the client starts over.

first_seq.description: The first event the view still holds, when it no longer holds every event from 0; a subscription from before it starts here.

from.description: First raw-log index, inclusive; 0 when absent.

to.description: Last raw-log index, inclusive; the end of the log when absent.

section.list.result.description: In the order they were made.

name.description: Core trims it and refuses with invalid_params one that is then blank, longer than 80 characters, or another section's, ignoring case.
Core trims it and refuses with invalid_params one that is then blank, longer than 80 characters, or another section's, ignoring case.

section.remove.params.description: Removes the section and puts its sessions in no section.

patch.description: A JSON merge patch (RFC 7386): objects merge, null deletes a key.

last_activity_at.description: The session's last_activity_at as session.list has it: when its latest turn ended; absent until one has. Every tile carries it, and a turn's end sends a tile even when the tile itself is unchanged.
